name: What the Flood Kept
description: An experimental neural-feed feature in which the viewer inhabits the perspective of a drowned city — specifically the pre-Meridian infrastructure beneath the Great Lakes corridor — experiencing time dilation across geological and human scales simultaneously. Director Yewande Sato-Mirković constructs the film as a meditation on erasure, using authentic pre-Collapse urban survey data to build the sensory environment. Viewers report experiencing duration as elastic, with some reporting the 90-minute runtime felt like decades.
cultural_impact: Sparked a significant public conversation about who owns historical data and whether the pre-Collapse city belongs to the corponations that built over it or to the people who still live in its footprint.
story_hooks: Hidden within the film's geological data layer are precise coordinates for a pre-Collapse structure that no corponation has officially acknowledged — something is still down there
The director received an anonymous data package after the film's release that she believes is the actual source of the survey data — and it contains more than geography
A Tier 1 resident who experienced the film claims the drowned neighborhood she inhabited during the runtime was her grandmother's actual street, which should be impossible
